thread:
maya-ops: Heads up — follow-up from last night's memory surge postmortem. I spun up a quick thread to align owners and next steps for remediation sprintboard. Link to postmortem: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/2025-03-memory-surge

alex-runtime: Thanks. TL;DR: recurring allocation drift in cache residency on long requests; reproduces in perf lab when running long-chained requests. We saw steady resident size growth vs baseline.

sam-sre: Can you paste the minimal repro and the pprof snippet? I've got CI machines free this afternoon.

maya-ops: repro: load test script with sustained 200qps, keys with 1-5k prefix reuse. pprof top: 54% arena alloc, 21% slab split, 10% kernel caches. snippet:
"""
pprof: CPU 30s
45.1% runtime.mallocgc
21.3% runtime.makeslice
8.2% custom/cache.(*Shard).retain
"""

alex-runtime: Also saw degraded eviction rate - our telemetry shows evict loop delaying GC by ~3x when residency crosses 28GB.

lina-eng: I can take instrumenting the retain path to log per-shard residency histograms. ETA EOW? Need 2 days to do safe rollout.

olivia-pm: Priority = P1 for Dedicated customers. Can we get remediation plan and owner assignments before Friday standup? PM will raise a sprint ticket.

maya-ops: Proposed actions:
- A1: Add per-shard residency histograms + rollout (owner: lina-eng, due: 2025-04-01)
- A2: Add soft-residency alert + auto-scale buffer (owner: alex-runtime, due: 2025-03-28)
- A3: GC tuning experiment + canary (owner: sam-sre, due: 2025-03-30)
- A4: Backfill failed evictions analysis + fix (owner: alex-runtime, due: 2025-04-05)
I'll create the sprintboard and link tickets.

alex-runtime: I'll take A2 and A4. For A2, suggest small early-warning metric: 7d growth slope > 1GB/day or spike >5GB in 10m triggers.

sam-sre: I'll run GC tuning matrix on lab nodes today and post results. If any config reduces allocation churn by >20% we can canary next week.

lina-eng: Quick question: do we want a short-lived feature flag for more aggressive shard compaction? Might help with fragmentation without GC changes.

maya-ops: Yes, feature flag sounds good. Add as subtask on A1: "compaction-flag".

olivia-pm: I'll create the epic and add acceptance criteria: "no P1 regressions for dedicated cluster for 14 days" and "alerting on slope + sudden spikes". Linking JIRA: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2024

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary for metrics instrumentation queued: infra-canary-172 -> prod-perf-lab. Check logs: https://ci.redwood/internal/172/logs

alex-runtime: Quick safety note: don't enable compaction flag globally until we validate tail-latency; compaction can stall write paths.

lina-eng: Agreed. I'll instrument latency gates and add a flag rollout plan in the ticket.

maya-ops: OK, I'll create the sprintboard now and assign tickets. Rough schedule:
- Mon: instrument + alerts in lab
- Tue-Wed: GC tuning experiments
- Thu: canary compaction flag + monitor
- Next Mon: full rollout decision

sam-sre: tagging followups: @alex-runtime, @lina-eng — please add test cases to avoid regressions.

alex-runtime: Will add unit + integration test stubs.

maya-ops: Thanks everyone. I'll post the sprintboard link here once created and ping again at Fri standup. :thumbsup:
